title: Create the server .env during init
description:
Server initialization fails at the "Migrate the database" task. The init playbook runs manage.py (migrate, then collectstatic) right after it clones the repo, and manage.py loads its settings from the .env file in the root of the repository. On a fresh server there is no .env yet, so DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE is unset and Django cannot load its settings. Today the only fix is to SSH in, write .env by hand, and rerun init.

Add a task to the init playbook, after the project is installed and before anything runs manage.py, that creates .env from .env.example when the file does not exist. Fill in only the values needed to boot on a server: DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=config.settings.prod, ENV, SUBDOMAIN (from the inventory's subdomain variable), and a newly generated SECRET_KEY, since the production settings refuse to start without one. Leave the other keys empty, so secrets (Clerk, Sentry, backup and other service credentials) are still entered by hand afterward. The task must never overwrite an existing .env, because it holds secrets entered by hand; rerunning init on a set-up server should leave .env untouched. Make the file readable only by the ubuntu user (mode 0600).

Update How to Set Up a Server for the First Time in docs/how-to.md to say init creates .env, and which keys still have to be filled in by hand before the first deploy.
acceptance_criteria:
- On a server with no .env, the init playbook creates one with DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE, ENV, SUBDOMAIN, and a generated SECRET_KEY set, and init runs past migrate and collectstatic.
- Rerunning init on a server that already has a .env leaves the file unchanged (the task reports ok, not changed).
- The created .env has the same keys as .env.example (just env-check would report no differences) and mode 0600.
- just infra-all passes.
- docs/how-to.md describes the new step and the keys left to fill in by hand.

title: Move server secrets to AWS Secrets Manager
description:
The server's secrets live only in a hand-edited .env file on each server. They have no backup or history, rotating one means SSHing in, and setting up a new server means finding every value again. Move the important ones into AWS Secrets Manager, in the stanford-clingen-projects account, so a server's .env can be rebuilt from one place.

Store one secret per Terraform workspace (tools/test and tools/prod), as JSON key-value pairs named after the .env keys. Terraform creates each secret and an IAM policy for reading it, but not its values, so the values never land in Terraform state; staff enter them in the AWS console. Secrets to move: SECRET_KEY, CLERK_SECRET_KEY, SENTRY_DSN, the backup writer's AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and the ETS's ETS_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and ETS_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. Values that aren't secret (DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE, ENV, SUBDOMAIN, SENTRY_ENV, bucket names) stay where they are.

How the server gets the values depends on the decision bead that blocks this one. This builds on tools-dd4, which creates .env during init; extend that work rather than adding a second way to write .env.

Update docs/how-to.md: how to add or change a secret, and how a server's .env gets its values.
acceptance_criteria:
- terraform validate passes, and terraform plan in each workspace shows the secret and its read policy, with no secret values in the plan or state.
- On a fresh server, init plus a deploy produces a working .env with every moved secret filled in, without hand-editing.
- Changing a value in Secrets Manager and following the documented steps updates the running app.
- just infra-all and just ci pass.
- docs/how-to.md covers adding, changing, and loading secrets.

title: Decide: read secrets from Secrets Manager at deploy time or run time?
description:
Moving the server's secrets to AWS Secrets Manager needs one decision first: where do the secrets get read?

Option 1 (recommended): at deploy time. Ansible runs on the developer's machine with that developer's AWS profile, reads the workspace's secret from Secrets Manager, and writes the server's .env (mode 0600). The server never needs AWS credentials to read secrets, and the app keeps reading .env as it does now. The trade-off: changing a secret takes a deploy (or rerunning the task that writes .env) before the app sees it.

Option 2: at run time. Django's settings fetch the secret from Secrets Manager with boto3 when the app starts. A secret change takes only a restart. The trade-off: Lightsail instances can't use IAM instance profiles, so the server needs a long-lived IAM access key in .env just to read the other secrets, which leaves a secret on disk anyway and adds an AWS call to every startup, including manage.py commands.

Which option should we use? Answer by closing this bead with the choice as the close reason.

title: Fix the Ansible task that installs uv
description: The Ansible task that installs uv (infra/ansible/tasks/install/uv.yml) runs `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh` with ansible.builtin.command. The command module does not run a shell, so the pipe is passed to curl as arguments and uv is never installed. Server initialization fails at this task, and uv has to be installed by hand on the server. Switch the task to ansible.builtin.shell so the pipe works. Keep become: false so uv installs into the ubuntu user's ~/.local/bin, where the deploy tasks expect it, and keep the creates guard so reruns skip it.
acceptance_criteria:
- The task uses ansible.builtin.shell, still runs as the ubuntu user, and keeps the creates guard.
- just infra-all passes (ansible-lint may need its noqa comment updated for the shell module).
- Running the init playbook on a server without uv installs it at ~/.local/bin/uv.

title: Give EmailTransfer a UUID and a short slug
description: Following the UUID convention in docs/design.md (shared bead tools-z53.9): EmailTransfer extends common.models.SlugModel with slug_prefix T, so its ID is a UUID and its slug looks like T3f2a9c1e instead of T000001. Remove its own slug field and save override. Nothing is deployed, so replace the ETS's migrations with one fresh initial migration.
acceptance_criteria: Tests first: the slug is T plus the first 8 hex characters of the UUID; it doesn't change on later saves; a colliding slug gets a new UUID and slug; history still records changes. README updated. just ci passes.
close_reason: EmailTransfer extends SlugModel with prefix T; its slug is now T + 8 hex chars of its UUID. Tests cover the slug format, stability across saves, collision retry, and history. Replaced the ETS migrations with a fresh 0001 (nothing deployed).

title: Use UUID primary keys for every model
description:
Decision (Liam, 2026-10-15): every ClinGen Tools model uses a UUID primary key instead of an auto-incrementing integer, so data from the standalone AS and CSS can move into the shared database without ID clashes, and IDs aren't guessable. Models with a human-readable slug use a type letter plus the first 8 hex characters of the UUID (like a short Git hash), such as T3f2a9c1e; on the rare collision, the model picks a new UUID. This replaces the HCI's zero-padded integer slugs (T000001) on purpose.

Add to the common app: an abstract UUIDModel (UUID primary key) and an abstract SlugModel (UUIDModel plus a unique slug built from a per-model prefix). UserProfile extends UUIDModel. Set SIMPLE_HISTORY_HISTORY_ID_USE_UUID so history rows use UUIDs too. Django's own models (User, sessions, admin log) keep their integer IDs. Nothing is deployed, so regenerate auth_'s initial migration instead of converting; developers reset their local tools.db. Document the convention in docs/design.md and AGENTS.md.
acceptance_criteria: Tests first: UUIDModel gives a UUID primary key; SlugModel builds prefix + 8 hex chars, keeps the slug on later saves, and picks a new UUID when the slug is taken; UserProfile and its history rows have UUID IDs. READMEs, docs/design.md, and AGENTS.md updated. just ci passes.
close_reason: Added common.models.UUIDModel and SlugModel (prefix + first 8 hex chars, new UUID on collision), moved UserProfile to UUIDModel, set SIMPLE_HISTORY_HISTORY_ID_USE_UUID, and regenerated auth_'s initial migration (nothing deployed). The history-ID setting also needed an ETS migration here. SlugModel's save and collision retry are tested through EmailTransfer in the next bead, since it's the first concrete slug model. Documented in docs/design.md and AGENTS.md.

title: Navigate the ETS with tabs
description: Liam's feedback: the ETS uses buttons to move between its pages, which looks odd. Use Bulma's boxed tabs (tabs is-boxed) for New Transfer and Past Transfers instead, with the current page's tab active (a transfer's page counts as Past Transfers). Every ETS page keeps the title and subtitle above the tabs.
acceptance_criteria: View tests: each page renders the title, subtitle, and both tabs, with the right tab active. README updated. just ci passes.
notes: Follow-up (Liam, 2026-10-15): a transfer's page gets its own active tab, 'Transfer <slug>', instead of marking Past Transfers active.
close_reason: Replaced the ETS's navigation buttons with boxed Bulma tabs in a shared header partial that also holds the title and subtitle, on the home, list, and detail pages. A transfer's page shows its ID as a smaller heading under the tabs, with Past Transfers active.

title: Use plain language in the ETS's pages
description:
Liam's feedback after trying the preview: ETS users aren't technical, so every page (the preview, the precondition failures, the flash messages, the transfer list and detail pages, the dry-run banner) should describe a transfer in plain language. Say 'sign-in account' for the Cognito user and 'GCI/VCI profile' for the DynamoDB user record, and never show PKs, Cognito usernames, attribute names like user_status, or raw AWS errors.

The technical details still have to be saved for developers: each step keeps its technical description and any raw error, and EmailTransfer saves the old and new Cognito usernames, the old record's PK, and the retired record's PK, if there was one. They're visible in the Django admin, not on the ETS's pages. Technical failures and AWS errors are also logged, so Sentry sees them.
acceptance_criteria: Tests first: step summaries and precondition failures name no PKs, usernames, or attribute names; the technical descriptions still do; a transfer saves the usernames and PKs; a failed step saves the raw error on the record but the detail page doesn't show it; AWS errors flash a plain message. README and docs/design.md updated if needed. just ci passes.
close_reason: Steps now have a plain summary (shown) and a technical description (saved). Precondition failures, the dry-run banner, status tags, and error messages are plain; AWS errors and the active-record case are logged. EmailTransfer saves the Cognito usernames and the moved and retired record PKs; each step saves its raw error.

title: Replace Sentry's deprecated send_default_pii with data_collection
description: sentry-sdk 2.72 deprecates the send_default_pii option in favor of data_collection, and every test run prints a DeprecationWarning from sentry_sdk.init() in src/config/settings/base.py. The HCI uses the same setting, so decide what we want Sentry to collect (user info, request bodies, and so on) and set data_collection explicitly instead of carrying over send_default_pii=True. See the docstring for data_collection in sentry_sdk/consts.py and https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/python/configuration/options/#data_collection.
acceptance_criteria:
- sentry_sdk.init() in settings/base.py uses data_collection and no longer passes send_default_pii.
- uv run pytest shows no Sentry DeprecationWarning.
- The src/config README says what Sentry collects.

title: Connect the ETS to real AWS on tools-test and prod
description:
Once the AWS-access decision is made, give the deployed ETS real credentials and try it.

- Create the ETS's IAM user in the account the decision names, with only the permissions docs/design.md lists. Whether it's managed in infra/terraform depends on the decision.
- Put the ETS environment variables in the tools-test .env (test user pool and table, if the decision provides them), then prod.
- On tools-test, run one real transfer end to end with test accounts, if test resources exist; otherwise do a preview-only check on prod with real accounts.
- Update docs/how-to.md with how to configure the ETS's credentials.
acceptance_criteria:
- The IAM policy allows only the actions and resources listed in docs/design.md.
- A preview against real data works on the deployed ETS.
- docs/how-to.md has a How to Configure ETS Credentials section.
notes: Set ETS_DRY_RUN=0 on each server only after a dry run there looks right.

title: Run a confirmed transfer and record each step
description:
Add the second half: when staff confirm a preview, run the transfer.

- Re-check the preconditions at confirm time, since the data may have changed since the preview.
- Save an EmailTransfer (status pending) before the first change, then run the steps in order: retire the requested-activation record if present, update the old record's email, disable the old Cognito user, enable the new one (skip if already enabled). Record each step's result on the EmailTransfer as it finishes.
- On the first failure, stop, mark the transfer failed, and store the error. Don't try to undo earlier steps.
- Show a detail page for the transfer with each step's result, and a list page of past transfers (django-tables2 if it's already ported, a plain table template otherwise).
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests for a full success, for the requested-activation path, and for a failure at each step (the later steps don't run, and the record shows which steps finished).
- A test that preconditions are re-checked on confirm.
- History records who ran each transfer.
- No test reaches AWS. just ci passes; docs/design.md updated if behavior changed.
notes: Include the ETS_DRY_RUN mode from the epic's notes: with it on, write steps are recorded as skipped (dry run) and none of the AWS write calls are made. Tests cover a dry run making no write calls.
close_reason: Confirming a preview re-checks the preconditions and runs run_transfer, which saves the EmailTransfer first, records each step's result as it goes, stops at the first failure, and in a dry run (ETS_DRY_RUN) records every step as skipped without writing. Added list and detail pages with plain tables (django-tables2 isn't ported).

title: Check preconditions and preview a transfer
description:
Add the first half of the transfer flow: staff enter the old and new emails, and the ETS checks the preconditions and shows what it would change, without changing anything.

- A form with old_email and new_email (both required, valid emails, and not equal).
- A preconditions function that uses clients.py and returns either a list of failures or the plan. Preconditions are listed in docs/design.md: old email has a Cognito user and a DynamoDB record; new email has a Cognito user; new email has no DynamoDB record or one with user_status 'requested activation'.
- The plan lists the steps that will run, with Cognito usernames and DynamoDB PKs, and notes when the new user is already enabled (that step is skipped).
- If a precondition fails, show every failure and no confirm button. Use flash messages only for errors, per the HCI convention.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests for the preconditions function covering every failure, the 'requested activation' case, any other user_status (fails), and the already-enabled case.
- View tests: invalid form, failed preconditions (no confirm button), and a valid preview that lists the steps.
- No test reaches AWS. just ci passes.
close_reason: Added TransferForm, check_preconditions returning a Preview (failures or a Plan with steps), and the preview on the ETS home page with a dry-run banner. Precondition failures render inline in red; AWS errors are error flash messages. Tests use FakeEtsClient instead of Stubber.

title: Add the ETS app, AWS client, and EmailTransfer model
description:
Create src/email_transfer_service/ and mount it at /ets/ (namespace ets) so it appears on the landing page.

- clients.py: a small wrapper around boto3 with functions for the calls the script makes: find a Cognito user by email (list_users with an email filter), find a DynamoDB user record by email (query item_type_index for item_type 'user', filtered by email, following LastEvaluatedKey), retire a record, update a record's email, and disable or enable a Cognito user. Settings come from env vars (add them to .env.example with dummy values): ETS_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ETS_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, ETS_AWS_REGION, ETS_COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID, ETS_DYNAMODB_TABLE_NAME. The decision bead on AWS access may rename these.
- models.py: EmailTransfer with old_email, new_email, the user who ran it, a status (pending, succeeded, failed), per-step results, an error message, and timestamps. Zero-padded slug like other ClinGen apps (T000001). django-simple-history on.
- A placeholder index view at /ets/ protected by has_ets_permissions.
- Add boto3 (and boto3-stubs for Cognito and DynamoDB if ty needs them).
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests for each client function using botocore Stubber, including DynamoDB pagination and the not-found cases.
- Model tests: slug generation and history.
- View tests: /ets/ returns 403 without has_ets_permissions and 200 with it; the landing page lists the ETS.
- just ci passes; README and docs.json updated.
close_reason: Added the email_transfer_service app at /ets/, EtsClient (boto3 low-level clients so Stubber covers every call), EmailTransfer with a dry_run flag, and a permission-gated index. Core's landing-page tests now build their URLconfs from the project's minus its tools.

title: Build the Email Transfer Service
description: Build the ETS at /ets/: a staff-facing form that moves a GCI or VCI user's account from an old email to a new one, replacing the hand-run update_email.py script. docs/design.md ('The Email Transfer Service') describes the behavior.
design:
Decisions:
- The behavior matches the update_email.py script: the same preconditions and the same four steps in the same order (retire a 'requested activation' record for the new email if there is one, point the old record at the new email, disable the old Cognito user, enable the new one). docs/design.md lists them.
- There is no override. The script's --force flag has no equivalent; a transfer that fails the preconditions needs a developer.
- Only users with UserProfile.has_ets_permissions can use the ETS (the shared epic adds the flag and mixin).
- Cognito and DynamoDB can't be changed atomically. An EmailTransfer record is saved before the first change, and each step's result is recorded as it runs. The run stops at the first failure.
- AWS settings (credentials, region, user pool ID, table name) come from the environment, never code. Tests never reach AWS: use botocore's Stubber.
- The Django app is src/email_transfer_service/, mounted at /ets/ with namespace ets.
- Where the AWS access comes from is undecided; see the decision bead that blocks wiring up real AWS.
notes:
Decision (Liam, 2026-10-14): get the ETS working locally first, doing dry runs only. ETS_DRY_RUN makes a confirmed transfer run the lookups and record every step, but skip the AWS writes; each write step is recorded as skipped (dry run) and the EmailTransfer has dry_run=True. Pages show a dry-run banner while it's on. tools-eap.4 turns it off on the servers once AWS access is decided. Locally, the ETS_ AWS vars point at the same account the update_email.py script uses, read-only in practice because dry run is on.

Update (Liam, 2026-10-15): ETS_DRY_RUN turns off only when it's exactly 0, matching the HCI's RUN_CONTRACT_TESTS=1 convention (0/1 flags across Liam's projects). Anything else, including empty, keeps dry run on.

title: Provision and deploy prod
description:
Repeat the tools-test bead for production at https://tools.clinicalgenome.org: terraform workspace new prod, the prod SSH key (~/.ssh/tools_ansible_prod_ed25519), the prod inventory entry, the prod .env, just server-prod-init, and just server-prod-deploy. The user runs the steps that create AWS resources.

Also record the backup reader credentials (backup_reader_* outputs, prod only) somewhere the team keeps secrets; the restore check that uses them is out of scope here. File follow-up beads for a CD workflow and uptime monitoring rather than doing them here.
acceptance_criteria:
- https://tools.clinicalgenome.org serves the landing page over HTTPS, and Clerk sign-in works.
- just server-prod-deploy succeeds and prints a pre-deployment backup name.
- Follow-up beads exist for CD and uptime monitoring.
- docs/how-to.md is updated if prod differed from test.

title: Provision and deploy tools-test
description:
Create the test infrastructure and deploy the app to https://tools-test.clinicalgenome.org. The user runs every step that creates AWS resources; the agent prepares commands, checks results, and fixes infra/ code when something fails.

Steps (docs/how-to.md has the details):
1. Prerequisite: main is pushed to https://github.com/ClinGen/tools (the user does this).
2. Create the tools_terraform_lock DynamoDB table (first time only).
3. Create ~/.ssh/tools_ansible_test_ed25519.
4. In infra/terraform: terraform init, terraform workspace new test, terraform apply. Commit .terraform.lock.hcl.
5. Copy infra/ansible/inventory.example.ini to inventory.ini and fill in the test IP.
6. Create the server's .env from .env.example: production settings, Clerk keys from the shared Clerk application, Sentry, and the backup credentials from terraform output (How to Configure Backup Credentials).
7. just server-test-init, then just server-test-deploy to confirm the pre-migration backup works.

Fix anything in infra/ or docs/how-to.md that turns out to be wrong along the way.
acceptance_criteria:
- https://tools-test.clinicalgenome.org serves the landing page over HTTPS.
- Signing in with Clerk works on tools-test.
- just server-test-deploy succeeds and prints a pre-deployment backup name, and manage.py listbackups on the server shows it.
- Requests for blocked paths (for example /.env) return 403.
- docs/how-to.md matches what was actually done, and just infra-all passes.

title: Add Sentry and S3 database backups
description:
Wire up Sentry and django-dbbackup so the deploy playbook's pre-migration backup works.

- Sentry: initialize in settings/base.py as hla-curation-interface/src/config/settings/base.py does, reading SENTRY_DSN and SENTRY_ENV. Tag every event with the tool that handled the request, taken from the resolved URL's namespace (as, css, ets, or none for the landing page), as docs/design.md describes.
- django-dbbackup: add the dependency and storage settings as the HCI does, reading DBBACKUP_BUCKET_NAME, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. Backups are compressed and named with SUBDOMAIN.
- Add every new variable to .env.example.
- infra/ansible/tasks/admin/django_dbbackup_predeploy.yml is already in place; confirm the command it runs works locally against a local filesystem storage in dev.
acceptance_criteria:
- A test checks that the tool tag is set from the URL namespace for a tool URL and is absent for /.
- A test checks that the dbbackup storage is configured from the environment variables.
- uv run src/manage.py dbbackup works in dev against local storage.
- just ci passes; .env.example and the src/config README are updated.
close_reason: Sentry init ported from the HCI, plus ToolTagMiddleware, which tags events with the tool's URL namespace (only for known tools). dbbackup and S3 storage ported from the HCI; local backups go to backups/. Verified manage.py dbbackup -o pre-deployment/... works locally, the same command the deploy runs. Kept send_default_pii for parity with the HCI and filed a chore to move to data_collection.

title: Add Clerk sign-in and per-tool permissions
description:
Port src/auth_ from hla-curation-interface/src/auth_ so staff sign in with Clerk, and add per-tool permissions.

- Port the ClerkBackend, UserProfile, sign-in and sign-out views, templates, and the Clerk JS. Drop HCI-only fields and checks (PHI agreement, curation and review permissions).
- UserProfile gets has_ets_permissions (BooleanField, default False). Later tools add their own flag the same way.
- auth_/permissions.py: a mixin and a decorator that take the name of a tool's flag, require a signed-in user, and return 403 if the flag isn't set. Example: ToolPermissionMixin with tool_permission = 'has_ets_permissions'.
- Register UserProfile in the Django admin so staff can grant the flag. Keep django-simple-history on UserProfile so grants are audited.
- Settings read CLERK_SECRET_KEY and CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY from the environment; add them to .env.example. The Clerk application is shared with other ClinGen apps (see the epic design).
- The landing page stays public; tools' pages are protected.
- Update the Authentication section of docs/design.md if the port differs from it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Port the HCI's auth_ tests that still apply, and add tests that: an anonymous user is redirected to sign-in from a protected view; a signed-in user without has_ets_permissions gets 403; a signed-in user with it gets 200; the landing page works for an anonymous user.
- Tests mock Clerk; none call Clerk's servers.
- just ci passes. src/auth_/README.md exists and docs.json lists it.
notes: Reworked to copy the HCI's Clerk sign-in as closely as possible, at the user's request: HCI views, JSX (hard-coded /auth/callback), templates, backend, navbar buttons, GET logout, profile page, os.environ for the Clerk keys, LOGIN_URL=/auth/login. Dropped the earlier next-URL handling, POST-only logout, and prod Clerk-key check.
close_reason: Ported Clerk sign-in from the HCI without PHI and curation permissions. UserProfile has has_ets_permissions; ToolPermissionMixin and tool_permission_required check a flag by name (an unknown name raises ImproperlyConfigured). Changes from the HCI: callback URL passed to the JS instead of hard-coded, login remembers a local next URL, logout is POST-only, prod refuses to start without the Clerk keys. Large diff (~1100 lines) kept as one PR because sign-in and permissions depend on each other.

title: Add the landing page and base layout

Add the page at / that links to each tool, plus the shared layout every tool's pages extend.

- src/core/: an app with a landing page view and template. The page lists each tool (AS at /as/, CSS at /css/, ETS at /ets/) with its one-line description from README.md. List only tools whose URLconf is mounted, so the page never links to a 404; until the ETS exists, the page may list no tools and should say so.
- src/templates/: base.html (Bulma, HTMX, a header with the site name, a footer) and error pages 403, 404, and 500. Adapt from clinvar-submission-service/src/templates.

- src/common/: only what this bead needs (for example, context processors). Port more of common later, when a tool needs it.
- WhiteNoise serves static files. Build URLs with {% url %}, never hard-coded paths.
- Add src/core, src/common, src/templates, and src/static to docs.json and scaffold their READMEs.

- Tests in src/core/tests.py: GET / returns 200 and renders the base layout; a mounted tool appears with a link built by reverse(); an unmounted tool does not appear; the empty state shows when no tools are mounted.
- Tests that the 404 and 500 handlers render their templates.
- just django-collectstatic and just ci pass.
- READMEs for every new directory, and docs.json updated.

The 500 page has no contact email because the team has no shared address yet. Fixed HTMX CSRF header name (X-CSRFToken; the CSS's X-CSRF-TOKEN isn't one Django reads).

title: Add the Django project skeleton
description:
Create the Django project in src/ so that just ci passes on an empty project.

- pyproject.toml modeled on clinvar-submission-service/pyproject.toml: project name clinvar-submission-service -> tools, same Ruff, coverage, pytest, and django-stubs config. Add django-dbbackup later (separate bead), not here.
- src/manage.py and src/config/ (urls.py, wsgi.py, settings/base.py, dev.py, test.py, prod.py) adapted from the CSS. Settings read SECRET_KEY, ENV, ALLOWED_HOSTS, and similar from the environment.
- .env.example at the root listing every variable the settings read, with dummy values.
- package.json, build.js, and biome.json adapted from the CSS so js-build and js-lint work.
- docs.json lists src/config, and src/config/README.md is scaffolded with uv run docs.py generate --directory src/config.
- README.md Getting Started: copy .env.example to .env.
acceptance_criteria:
- A test in src/config/tests.py checks that the test settings load and that Django's system check passes.
- uv sync, npm ci, and just ci all pass.
- .env.example exists and README.md tells you to copy it.
- docs.json and src/config/README.md are up to date.
close_reason: Added pyproject, layered settings (prod refuses to start without SECRET_KEY), JS build, .env.example, and src/config README. Test settings use plain static storage so tests don't need collectstatic.

title: Stand up ClinGen Tools on tools-test and prod
description: Build the shared Django project that every tool runs in, and deploy it to tools-test.clinicalgenome.org and then tools.clinicalgenome.org. When this epic is done, the landing page is live, staff can sign in with Clerk, and the ETS epic can start.
design:
docs/design.md describes the architecture; this epic builds its shared parts.

Decisions:
- Base the skeleton on the CSS (clinvar-submission-service/src: config, core, common, templates, static) and port auth_ from the HCI (hla-curation-interface/src/auth_), which already uses Clerk. Adapt, don't copy blindly: drop HCI-only concepts such as the PHI agreement and curation permissions.
- Staff sign in with Clerk. We share an existing ClinGen Clerk application with other apps rather than creating a new one, so the Clerk keys come from that application. Keys live only in .env files, never in code or beads.
- Permissions are per tool. UserProfile gets one boolean flag per tool (starting with ETS), and each tool's views check their own flag through a mixin in auth_. Staff grant flags in the Django admin.
- Infrastructure is already written in infra/ (Terraform and Ansible, copied from the HCI). Beads here may fix it but shouldn't redesign it.
- The repo is public at https://github.com/ClinGen/tools, so the server clones over HTTPS. The server can only deploy what has been pushed to main; pushing is the user's call.
- The user runs terraform apply and anything else that creates billed AWS resources. Agents prepare the commands and stop.

title: Decide where the ETS gets its AWS access
description:
The ETS changes GCI and VCI user accounts in an AWS Cognito user pool and the GeneVariantCuration DynamoDB table (see 'The Email Transfer Service' in docs/design.md). Before we can build or deploy it, we need answers to these questions:

1. Which AWS account holds the GCI/VCI Cognito user pool and the GeneVariantCuration table?
2. Who creates the ETS's IAM user in that account, and is it managed by Terraform in this repo or elsewhere? The design calls for least privilege: list, enable, and disable users in the one user pool, and query and update items in the one table.
3. Does the ETS on tools-test need to reach a test user pool and table, so we can try transfers without touching production data? If so, which ones?
4. What are the names of the environment variables for the credentials, region, user pool ID, and table name, and where are the values kept?

The ETS reads all of these from the environment, never from code.
